raw_text:
Here’s a concise, trainer-ready 12-week postpartum plan summary combining strength, core, cardio, and breastfeeding-supportive nutrition. It honors “light only” through week 6 postpartum, then progresses intensity so she feels notably stronger by Week 12. Home-based, yoga mat only; optional light external load from Week 9 if symptom-free.

Global guardrails
- Clearance: Light activity only until 6-week OB check; progress after clearance.
- Green lights: No doming/coning, pelvic heaviness/leakage, incision pain, or increased bleeding; steady breathing (no Valsalva). Exhale on effort.
- RPE targets: 2–4 through Week 6; 4–6 Weeks 7–10; 5–7 Weeks 11–12.
- Frequency: Strength 3 days/week (nonconsecutive); cardio 3–5 days/week; mobility/breathing most days.

Weekly template
- Each strength day: 3–5 min 360° breathing + pelvic floor; dynamic mobility; full-body session; short core finisher (as indicated); cool-down breathing.
- Cardio: Walking-based with intervals added progressively; low-impact HIIT possible after Week 12 if all readiness boxes are ticked.
- Core woven into every session; direct abs progressions begin after Week 6 per below.

Phase 1: Weeks 1–2 (postpartum weeks 4–6) — Early recovery, light only
- Objective: Reconnect breath/pelvic floor, circulation, posture; easy walking.
- Strength (2–3x/week; 10–20 min; bodyweight)
  - Glute bridge mini range 2–3 x 6–8
  - Side-lying clamshell 2 x 8–10/side
  - Chair box squat (partial) 2 x 6–8
  - Wall angels or Y-T-W 2 x 6–8
  - Very high-incline wall push-up 1–2 x 6–8 (only if symptom-free)
- Core (safe early)
  - 360° breathing + gentle pelvic floor lifts 2–3 sets/day
  - Heel slides or supine marching feet down 1–2 x 6–8/side
- Cardio
  - Walk 10–25 minutes most days, flat terrain, RPE 2–3.
- Notes: Stop if incision pulling, pelvic heaviness, leakage, dizziness, or increased bleeding.

Phase 2: Weeks 3–4 (postpartum weeks 6–8; after OB clearance) — Foundations
- Objective: Low-load core re-entry; reinforce squat/hinge/push mechanics.
- Strength (3x/week; 25–30 min)
  - Squat to chair (3-sec down) 3 x 8–10
  - Bridge (3–1–3 or 5-sec hold) 3 x 8–10
  - Hip hinge to wall 3 x 8–10
  - Incline push-up 2–3 x 8–12
  - Side-lying hip abduction or clamshell 2–3 x 10–12/side
- Core
  - Dead bug arms → arm + single heel slide 2–3 x 6–8/side
  - Modified side plank (knees) 10–20 sec x 2–3/side
  - Tall-kneeling anti-extension plank prep (hands elevated) 5–8 x 5–8 sec
- Cardio
  - 4–5 days/week: 25–40 min steady at RPE 3–4; 1 day add 3 x 45–60 sec brisk (RPE 5) with 3 min easy between.

Phase 3 intensified: Weeks 5–6 (postpartum weeks 8–10) — Build strength and capacity
- Objective: Unilateral patterns, tempos, short rests; stronger core isometrics.
- Strength (3x/week; 30–35 min; supersets)
  - A1 Squat to box or goblet hold (light if available) 3–4 x 10–12 @ 3–1–1
  - A2 Incline push-up 3–4 x 10–12
  - B1 Hip hinge (slow 4-sec eccentric) 3–4 x 8–10
  - B2 Side plank (knees) 3 x 20–30 sec/side
  - C1 Split squat (short ROM) 2–3 x 8–10/side
  - C2 Bridge march or supported single-leg bridge 2–3 x 8–10/side
  - C3 Bird dog (2–3 sec hold) 2–3 x 8/side
- Core emphasis: Breathing/bracing before each big lift; no coning.
- Cardio
  - Intervals: 6–8 x 60 sec brisk (RPE 5) / 2–3 min easy (25–35 min total)
  - 1–2 steady days 30–40 min RPE 3–4; optional gentle hills if symptom-free.

Phase 4 intensified: Weeks 7–8 (postpartum weeks 10–12) — Strength endurance, longer core holds
- Objective: Circuits, single-leg control, anti-rotation under fatigue.
- Strength (3x/week; circuits 3 rounds; 60–90 sec rest)
  - Goblet squat to parallel 10–12 @ 3–1–1
  - Hip hinge/RDL (tempo or light load) 10–12
  - Split squat supported 8–10/side
  - Push-up progression (lower surface) 8–12
  - Side plank staggered knees/feet 20–30 sec/side
  - Tall/half-kneeling anti-rotation hand-press 8–10/side with 3–5 sec holds
  - Optional: Hip thrust (couch) 12–15 with 2–3 sec squeeze; step-ups 10/side
- Core finisher 2 days/week
  - Incline forearm plank 20–30 sec x 2 OR dead bug contralateral 8–10/side
- Cardio
  - Intervals: 8–10 x 60–75 sec brisk (RPE 5–6) / 2 min easy
  - Tempo: 15 min at RPE 4–5 within a 25-min session
  - Steady: 35–45 min RPE 3–4; optional short hill session if symptom-free.

Phase 5 intensified: Weeks 9–10 (postpartum weeks 12–14) — Light-moderate loading, capacity
- Objective: Push strength safely; anti-rotation with load; maintain quality.
- Strength (3x/week; 35–40 min; 4-round supersets if possible)
  - 1A Goblet squat 8–10 (5–20 lb if available; otherwise tempo)
  - 1B Push-up (lower incline) 8–12
  - 2A RDL with light-moderate load 8–10 @ 3–1–1
  - 2B Half-kneeling anti-rotation press (isometric or light load) 8–10/side
  - 3A Step-up to knee balance holding light load 8–10/side
  - 3B Dead bug full 8–10/side
  - Accessory day option: Single-leg hinge to wall touch 8–10/side; hip thrust 12–15; side plank 20–30 sec/side
- Cardio
  - Intervals: 6–8 x 2 min brisk (RPE 5–6) / 2 min easy
  - Tempo: 20 min at RPE 4–5 within a 30-min session
  - Long steady: 45–60 min RPE 3–4.

Phase 6 intensified: Weeks 11–12 (postpartum weeks 14–16) — Feel strong and fit
- Objective: Confident single-leg work, stronger push-ups, resilient core; RPE 5–7.
- Strength (3x/week; 40 min; supersets)
  - Block 1: Goblet squat to parallel 10–12 + push-up to sturdy chair 8–12
  - Block 2: RDL (load or tempo) 8–10 + dead bug with heel hover 8–10/side
  - Block 3: Split squat (load or 4-sec eccentric) 8–10/side + side plank with top-leg raise 6–8/side or 25–35 sec
  - Finisher (1–2 days): Tall-kneeling front plank on couch 15–25 sec x 2–3 OR suitcase carry (light) 2 x 30–40 m/side
- Cardio
  - Intervals: 5–7 x 3 min brisk (RPE 6) / 2 min easy
  - Tempo: 25 min at RPE 4–5 within 35 min
  - Long steady: 50–65 min RPE 3–4
  - Optional hills: 6–8 x 60–75 sec up (RPE 5–6) if zero symptoms past 2 weeks

Core progression milestones (when to add “abs”)
- Weeks 1–2: Breathing + pelvic floor; heel slides; mini bridges
- Weeks 3–4: Dead bug arms → arm + heel slide; modified side plank; short incline plank holds
- Weeks 5–6: Dead bug contralateral (short range); longer side plank holds; incline forearm plank 10–20 sec
- Weeks 7–8: Anti-rotation holds; bird dog 8–10/side; incline plank 15–25 sec
- Weeks 9–12: Full dead bug, side plank feet/staggered, tall-kneeling front plank 15–25 sec; optional floor forearm plank 10–20 sec by Weeks 11–12 if all green lights

HIIT guidance (post-program add-on)
- Timing: Earliest 12–16+ weeks postpartum if symptom-free with Week 12 cardio and strength benchmarks; cleared by OB.
- Start with low-impact HIIT: 6–8 x 30–45 sec hard (RPE 6–7) / 90 sec easy on hill-walk, bike, or elliptical. Max 1–2 days/week, 48+ hours apart.

Nutrition summary for breastfeeding support
- Energy: +300–500 kcal/day above baseline; adjust to hunger, weight, and milk supply.
- Protein: 1.6–2.0 g/kg/day across 4–5 meals/snacks.
- Carbs: 45–55% calories, focus on complex sources for training energy.
- Fats: 25–35% calories, prioritize omega-3s (200–300 mg DHA/day via low-mercury fish 2–3x/week or algae supplement).
- Hydration: 3.0–3.5 L/day; add 250–500 mL on hot or high-output days.
- Micronutrients: Continue prenatal; ensure vitamin D, iodine (150 mcg), choline (450–550 mg), calcium (~1,000 mg), iron per labs.
- Simple plate: Half veg/fruit, quarter protein, quarter whole grains/starchy veg, plus 1–2 thumbs healthy fats. Protein + produce/carb for snacks.
- Pre/post training: Small carb + protein pre-intervals if hungry; 20–30 g protein + carbs within 1–2 hours post.

Weekly layout example
- Mon: Strength + easy walk
- Tue: Intervals (progress per phase)
- Wed: Strength + recovery walk
- Thu: Steady/tempo walk
- Fri: Strength + short core finisher
- Sat: Long steady walk or family hills (if cleared)
- Sun: Rest or gentle mobility/breath

Readiness to advance after Week 12
- Can do: 10–12 goblet squats to parallel with light–moderate load; 8–12 low-incline push-ups; 30-sec side plank/side symptom-free; balanced single-leg hinges and split squats.
- Next steps: Gradually increase external load (5 lb steps), add bands (rows, Pallof), introduce supported floor planks 20–30 sec, and consider 1 low-impact HIIT day/week. Delay running/high-impact until passing a postpartum run-readiness screen and staying symptom-free 24–48 hours after trial runs.

This integrates all modalities into a single, progressive plan that protects healing while pushing intensity appropriately so she feels strong and fit by Week 12. Adjust week-to-week based on sleep, energy, and any symptom feedback.
